payload.title: 15 Engagement Ring Styles and Who Each One Suits
payload.audience: Couples in their 30s, affluent, interested in destination weddings and luxury celebrations, AUD 150k+ budget
payload.reader: A couple in their mid 30s, about to propose or newly engaged, well travelled and design literate, who have scrolled endless ring photos and now want a clear way to match a style to the person who will wear it every day, including on the flight to and the week of a wedding abroad.
payload.goal: Click through to the destinations hub to start picturing where the wedding could happen (Wedded Concierge enquiry at /wonderland-concierge as secondary CTA).
payload.angle: Most style roundups are photo galleries that name a look and stop there; this one judges every style against the same four 'who it suits' lenses: personality and taste, everyday lifestyle, hand and finger shape, and how it travels and photographs at a destination wedding (sun, salt water, long-haul flights, ceremony close-ups). Each of the 15 styles gets a plain-words description, a 'suits you if' line, a 'think twice if' line and a pointer to the sister settings guide where the stone-holding mechanics matter, so a couple can shortlist two or three styles before they ever walk into a jeweller.
must_include: A short 'how to use this guide' intro naming the four lenses applied to every style: personality, lifestyle, hand and finger, travel and destination wedding
Style 1: Classic solitaire (single centre stone; suits minimalists and those who want a ring that never dates; flatters most hands; pairs with almost any wedding band; easy to wear on travel days)

Style 2: Halo (centre stone ringed by smaller stones; suits those who love sparkle and a bigger face-up look; flatters shorter fingers by adding presence; think twice for hands-on work or frequent snorkelling)
Style 3: Hidden halo (small stones under the centre, visible from the side; suits people who want a clean top view with a private detail; reads beautifully in side-profile ceremony photos)
Style 4: Three-stone (centre plus two side stones, often read as past, present, future; suits sentimental couples; works well on longer fingers and wider hands)
Style 5: Toi et moi (two stones side by side, often different shapes or colours; suits couples who want a story about two people; strong personality piece; consider band pairing early)
Style 6: East-west (elongated stone set horizontally; suits the understated contrarian; sits lower across the finger and can make short fingers look wider, long fingers more balanced)
Style 7: Cluster (several small stones grouped to form one shape; suits those who love texture and a floral or vintage feel; can give a larger look without a single large stone)
Style 8: Vintage or antique-inspired (milgrain, engraving, filigree; suits lovers of history and romance; detail work needs gentle care on beach and resort days)
Style 9: Art deco (geometric lines, step-cut shapes, strong symmetry; suits architectural and fashion-led taste; photographs crisply in black and white and in strong Mediterranean light)
Style 10: Pavé band (small stones set along the band; suits those who want sparkle all the way round; flag that small stones need periodic checks and link the sister post for setting detail)

Style 11: Bezel style (metal rim framing the stone; suits active, outdoorsy and practical wearers; modern or retro depending on metal; one or two lines only, then link the sister settings post for mechanics)
Style 12: Split shank (band divides as it meets the centre; suits those who want a bolder statement and to balance a larger stone; flatters longer, slimmer fingers)
Style 13: Eternity-style (stones running part or all of the way round; suits those who want the band itself to be the statement; note resizing considerations in general terms without figures)
Style 14: Bypass or contemporary (asymmetric, wrap or open designs; suits creative, design-led wearers who want something unexpected; check how it sits beside a wedding band)

Style 15: Coloured gemstone centre (sapphire, emerald, ruby and others; suits individualists and couples marking heritage or a meaningful place; durability notes in plain words only, sourced to GIA or equivalent)
Each style: a one-line 'suits you if' and a one-line 'think twice if', covering personality, lifestyle, hand and finger, and travel and destination wedding
A brief hand and finger section in general terms (proportion, finger length, knuckle size) with no body-shaming language, gender-neutral

A short travel and destination wedding section: wearing and photographing the ring abroad, when to swap to a plain band, carrying it securely, and checking that jewellery insurance covers overseas travel (general advice, no figures)
Exactly 4 one-sentence Key takeaways
Soft bridge to the destination wedding: link to /destinations (primary) and /wonderland-concierge (secondary), using only claims from brand-facts.md

Internal links (both ways with the sister post): /style-advice/engagement-ring-setting-for-active-lifestyle, plus /2026-engagement-ring-trends-amaree-jewellery, /expert-advice/how-much-should-you-spend-on-an-engagement-ring, /expert-advice/proposal-ideas (the old 45-proposal-ideas URL redirects here), /proposal/how-to-propose-a-step-by-step-guide-to-the-perfect-moment, /the-top-proposal-destinations-in-italy, /proposal-destinations-in-new-zealand
Reuse and re-check GIA-sourced facts from content/posts/engagement-ring-setting-for-active-lifestyle/03-source-pack.json for any durability or gemstone statement
avoid: Any price figures or price ranges (rings, stones, resizing, insurance or weddings)
Naming or recommending jewellers or brands (the Amaree trends post may be internally linked but not presented as an endorsement)
Settings mechanics in depth (prong counts, head heights, snag tests); keep to one line and link the sister settings post
Cathedral as a standalone style (it is a setting profile covered in the sister post)
Gendered assumptions about who proposes or who wears the ring; use 'the wearer' or 'your partner'
Body-shaming or prescriptive language about hands and fingers ('fix', 'hide', 'slim down'); frame as proportion and preference
Invented statistics or trend percentages (e.g. 'X% of couples choose a halo') unless sourced
Copying wording, structure or images from jewellers or competitors, including Easy Weddings
Claims that any style is 'unbreakable' or guarantees a stone will never be lost
Business details not in brand-facts.md (fees, a named Advisor, Wedded Privileges specifics are deferred)
Em dashes and US spelling (use jewellery, colour, travelling)
